v.w: It marks the configuration class, turns on auto-configuration and scans the package of the class and its sub-packages.

v.q: Which annotation is NOT part of @SpringBootApplication?
v.w: It combines configuration, auto-configuration and component scanning.

v.q: How does Spring Boot auto-configuration decide what to set up?
o: It checks the classpath, beans and properties via `@Conditional` rules
It reads a hidden file listing which beans to create
It asks the developer questions at startup
It scans the file system for installed databases
v.w: For example, with `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa` and a datasource on the classpath, it configures `EntityManagerFactory`. Your own bean usually wins via `@ConditionalOnMissingBean`.

v.q: Which annotation is a typical auto-configuration condition?
v.w: It backs off when you define your own bean, so your configuration wins.

v.q: What is a Spring Boot starter?
o: A dependency bundle that pulls in a consistent set of libraries
A class that contains the `main` method of an application
A command-line tool that generates the project folders
A plugin that restarts the server when code changes
v.w: `spring-boot-starter-web` brings Spring MVC, Jackson and embedded Tomcat with compatible versions managed by the Boot BOM.

v.q: Which statement about starters is NOT true?
o: A starter contains the main method
v.w: The main method is in your own application class. A starter is only a dependency bundle.

v.q: A property is defined in `application.properties`, an environment variable and a command-line argument. Which wins?
o: The command-line argument, which has the highest precedence
The properties file, because it is read first
The environment variable, because it is global
Whichever of them was defined first
v.w: Order, high to low (simplified): command-line args, environment variables, profile-specific files, `application.properties`, defaults.

v.q: Which source has the highest precedence for a property?
v.w: Command-line arguments override environment variables, which override files.

v.q: How do you activate different configuration per environment?
o: Edit the source code and rebuild it for each environment
Rename the JAR file differently for every environment
Keep a separate Git branch for each of the environments
v.w: One artefact runs everywhere, with configuration injected from outside. Never commit secrets: use environment variables or a vault.

v.q: Which setting activates the prod profile?
v.w: The active profile selects application-prod properties and profile-specific beans.

v.q: What does Spring Boot Actuator provide?
o: Production endpoints such as health, metrics and info
A visual designer that lets you draw your controllers
Automatic database migrations that run on each startup
A replacement runtime that is used instead of the JVM
v.w: Expose only what you need, and secure the endpoints. Health groups feed Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes.

v.q: Which Actuator endpoint do Kubernetes probes usually call?
v.w: The health endpoint, with liveness and readiness groups, is made for probes. Do not expose the others publicly.

v.q: A bean has a constructor with its dependencies. How should they be injected?
o: Constructor injection: dependencies are explicit, final and testable
Field injection with `@Autowired` on each private field
Static setter methods that are called from `main`
Calling `new` for each dependency inside the class itself
v.w: Constructor injection makes dependencies explicit, supports immutability and works without the container in unit tests.

v.q: Which injection style is best for mandatory dependencies?
v.w: Constructor injection makes dependencies explicit and lets tests create the object without Spring.

v.q: How does a Boot app typically run as a single deployable?
o: An executable JAR with an embedded server such as Tomcat
A WAR that only a shared application server can run
Source code compiled on the server at start
A Docker image that contains no JVM
v.w: `java -jar app.jar` starts the embedded server. A WAR is still possible but optional.

v.q: Which statement about a Spring Boot executable jar is NOT true?
o: It needs a shared application server
v.w: A fat jar carries its own server, so no external application server is needed.
